# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer and mail carrier  <sub>[v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a low-statured, heavy-set man who is lacking hair. He has a round face with prominent blue eyes. When relaxing on his veranda in the evenings, he is often seen smoking his pipe.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056)_

## Personality

Known for his blunt and candid nature, he regularly voices his exact thoughts without hesitation. He can be impetuous and critical, yet he also demonstrates supportive and pleasant qualities toward those he befriended. He resents receiving pity from others and maintains strong opinions on matters ranging from marriage to literary works.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072)_

## Traits

- candid and direct  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>
- impetuous  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>
- exacting and critical  <sub>[v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041)</sub>
- dislikes being pitied  <sub>[v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078)</sub>

## History

After relocating from New Brunswick, he acquired a property next to the Abernethy farm in Brierley. He initially maintained an independent bachelor household, hiring John Henry Carter as a helper. He formed a warm friendship with Nell, often exchanging visits with her and listening to her news. Following a deathbed promise made to his sister in Scottsford, he proposed to Emily Scott, who accepted and relocated with him. Though he and Emily experienced domestic friction over housekeeping standards and his parrot Nutmeg, he settled into married life. He offered blunt advice and editorial feedback on Nell's writing efforts and subsequently took on duties delivering local mail.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P72](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0072), [v3 c18 P24](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0024)_

## Background by volume

- relocated from Scottsford, New Brunswick to Brierley  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- routinely punished by his schoolmaster as a youth  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>
- received his parrot Nutmeg from his late brother, a sailor  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- remained a bachelor for many years before marrying later in life  <sub>[v2 c17 P77](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0077), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Ignore that parrot. He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

> Tut, tut, miss, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur. On occasion, I am overly impetuous myself, miss . . . much too impetuous. However, I am unable to refrain from voicing my exact thoughts, and people are required to accept me as I am. Now, had that cow gotten into my cabbages . . . yet do not dwell on it, she did not, hence everything is fine. Because you wish to dispose of her, I believe I would prefer taking your cow in trade.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> It isn't right, not right whatsoever, Nell. ‘Spare the rod and spoil the child.’ Back when I attended school, the master flogged me routinely each day on the grounds that if I was not causing trouble at that moment, I was planning it.  <sub>[v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036)</sub>

> That old bother Agatha Sowerby dropped by once more today, nagging me to contribute money for purchasing a vestry room carpet. My hatred for that woman exceeds my feelings for anyone else I am acquainted with. In merely six words, she is capable of compressing an entire sermon—complete with text, commentary, and application—and launching it at your head as if it were a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> I do not believe in delaying marriage for too long—as I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
